subject: physical-education

location.unitTitle: Aquatics, Alternative, and Adapted Activity Options

standardsMappingAuthority.note: Standards remain governed by the bound production package.

instructions: Complete the safe activity or accessible equivalent and document the requested performance evidence.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing trouble, unsafe conditions, or missing adult supervision.

learnerTasks.prompt: Explain the critical features or key principle of water safety and aquatic activity where access exists in your own words.
Demonstrate or fully describe adapted and parasport activity forms using a version your body and setting allow. A described or adapted version earns full credit.
Apply alternative activities: climbing, martial arts, skating, and others in a new situation and explain the decision or adjustment you made.
Analyze a plausible technique fault, tactical error, or unsafe choice involving equipment adaptation and rule modification; correct it and explain why.
Connect access barriers: cost, transport, facility, and staffing with trying an activity form that is unfamiliar and reflecting honestly and explain how one affects the other.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Trial two activity forms new to the learner — at least one adapted or alternative form — and produce an access analysis identifying what would make each sustainable.
Identify one thing you can now do or direct yourself, one adjustment that improved it, and one next goal you set for yourself.

learnerSuccessCriteria: Provide evidence that meets the stated safe participation and self-management criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated skill cues or movement quality criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated tactical or training reasoning criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated self-assessment and revision criterion.
accommodations: Access supports may change format, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. An adapted or described performance is full credit, not partial credit.

provenance.unitObjective: How can the learner demonstrate the goals of Aquatics, Alternative, and Adapted Activity Options?
